explanation: Binary search the interval from zero to max(1,x). Compare middle with x/middle to avoid overflow from squaring; stop when floating-point rounding prevents further interval refinement.
timeComplexity: O(log(R/ε)) refinements for initial width R and attained absolute precision ε, bounded by 1100 iterations for doubles. Every refinement halves the bracket, with at most 1100 iterations in the displayed implementation.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only the bracket endpoints, midpoint and iteration counter are stored.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: For x>0, the initial interval [0,max(1,x)] contains √x. For a positive midpoint, midpoint≤x/midpoint is equivalent to midpoint²≤x without overflowing a square. Replacing the appropriate endpoint preserves containment. Repeated bisection narrows the bracket until floating-point resolution prevents further progress.
walkthrough: For x=6.25, start with [0,6.25]. Midpoint 3.125 exceeds 6.25/3.125=2, so the root lies below it. Repeated comparisons narrow the interval around 2.5, whose square is 6.25; return approximately 2.5.
edgeCases: x=0 returns zero without dividing by a midpoint.
Values between zero and one still use an upper bound of one.
Division avoids overflow when x is very large.
The judge compares floating-point answers with a relative tolerance.
